## Database gate

- Official Migration `232_channel_cache_write_1h_pricing.sql` adds nullable
  `NUMERIC(20,12)` `cache_write_1h_price` columns to four channel-pricing tables;
  no backfill is performed and `NULL` retains legacy pricing behavior.
- Official Migrations `232_group_force_openai_fast.sql`,
  `232_group_reasoning_effort_over_limit.sql`, and
  `233_group_free_openai_fast.sql` add three non-null group policy columns with
  backward-compatible defaults (`false`, `downgrade`, and `false`).
- The migration runner keys applied migrations by full filename, so the three
  official `232_*` files do not collide with Custom
  `232_subscription_plan_renewal_policy.sql`; all five files have distinct
  `schema_migrations.filename` values and deterministic lexical order.
- All four official migrations are transactional and additive. They use
  `ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS`; no destructive DDL, data rewrite, index rebuild,
  or `CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY` is introduced.
- Program rollback to `v0.1.185-custom.5` remains compatible because the old
  binary ignores the added columns. Database rollback is forward-only: retain
  the new columns and migration rows instead of dropping them.
- Before installation, back up `groups`, the four channel-pricing tables,
  `subscription_plans`, and `schema_migrations`; validate the bundled migrations
  on a PostgreSQL copy. No production DDL or DML was executed during this review.

Read-only production check:

```sql
SELECT table_name, column_name, data_type, is_nullable, column_default
FROM information_schema.columns
WHERE table_schema = 'public'
  AND (
    (table_name = 'groups' AND column_name IN (
      'force_openai_fast',
      'free_openai_fast',
      'max_reasoning_effort_over_limit'
    ))
    OR
    (table_name IN (
      'channel_model_pricing',
      'channel_pricing_intervals',
      'channel_account_stats_model_pricing',
      'channel_account_stats_pricing_intervals'
    ) AND column_name = 'cache_write_1h_price')
  )
ORDER BY table_name, column_name;

SELECT filename, checksum, applied_at
FROM schema_migrations
WHERE filename IN (
  '232_channel_cache_write_1h_pricing.sql',
  '232_group_force_openai_fast.sql',
  '232_group_reasoning_effort_over_limit.sql',
  '232_subscription_plan_renewal_policy.sql',
  '233_group_free_openai_fast.sql'
)
ORDER BY filename;
```

Manual migration SQL: none. The reviewed, embedded Migration files are the
authoritative forward migration and are applied under the repository advisory
lock on application startup.

## Conflict and custom-impact review

- Regenerated Ent from the combined Schema so Custom `minimum_balance` and the
  official OpenAI Fast/reasoning fields coexist in entity, mutation, runtime,
  create/update, and migration descriptors.
- Kept Custom group model blocklists while copying the official
  `max_reasoning_effort_over_limit` field in group duplication.
- Advanced API-key auth snapshots to official version `22` while retaining
  Custom model blocklist, long-context pricing, and model-pricing fields.
- Kept Custom `minimum_balance` in group create/update payloads and added the
  official normalized `force_openai_fast` and `free_openai_fast` payloads.
- Reviewed every listed shadow source against its mapped Custom target; the
  Custom moderation, model-access, billing, payment, renewal, and channel
  monitoring implementations remain authoritative and reachable.

## Regression plan

- Backend Unit, Integration, production build, Wire generation, incremental
  lint, and migration tests run in the trusted upgrade gate.
- Frontend typecheck, Custom Vitest, and production build run in the same gate.
- Candidate Tree delta, thin-bridge, shadow-map, database-boundary, Release
  preflight, and exact-SHA CI remain hard publication gates.
- Runtime acceptance after publication must cover API-key cache refresh, group
  create/duplicate/update, Standard/Fast billing, OpenAI reasoning over-limit,
  channel 1h cache pricing, payment callbacks, subscription renewal, and local
  and manual fulfillment.
